notes.front: What is the Amateur Radio Service, in one sentence?
notes.back: A radio service for self-training, communication between amateurs and technical investigation, done out of personal interest and not for money.
notes.explanation: Every rule in this deck belongs to it, and the rule’s phrase “without pecuniary interest” (no financial gain) is why business use is excluded.
notes.example: Talking to another amateur across town, or building and testing your own antenna, is what the service is for; running a taxi dispatch over it is not.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is the FCC, in one sentence?
notes.back: The Federal Communications Commission: the US agency that regulates and enforces the Amateur Radio Service rules.
notes.explanation: Its amateur rules are in Title 47 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 97, which the exam draws on.
notes.example: The FCC issues your licence and call sign, and can inspect your station or suspend your licence.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What is an amateur licence class, in one sentence?
notes.back: A level of amateur licence; the class on your licence grant sets which privileges you may use.
notes.explanation: New licences are issued in three classes: Technician (this exam), General and Amateur Extra.
notes.example: A Technician and an Amateur Extra licensee may use different frequencies, because their classes differ.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is the ULS, in one sentence?
notes.back: The FCC's Universal Licensing System: the database that records every amateur licence grant.
notes.explanation: A licence exists when it appears in the ULS; that record, not a paper, is the proof.
notes.example: After you pass, you look yourself up in the ULS to see whether your grant and call sign have appeared.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a CSCE, in one sentence?
notes.back: A Certificate of Successful Completion of an Examination: proof that you passed exam elements.
notes.explanation: It gives you credit for the elements it shows for 365 days, but it is not a licence grant.
notes.example: Passing the Technician exam earns a CSCE showing that element; the licence itself comes later, when it appears in the ULS.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a call sign, in one sentence?
notes.back: The unique identifier shown on your station's licence grant, used to identify the station over the air.
notes.explanation: Each new station licence shows one unique call sign, chosen by one of the FCC's call sign systems.
notes.example: When a station says its call sign on the air, listeners know exactly which licensed station is transmitting.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is the sequential call sign system, in one sentence?
notes.back: The FCC picks your call sign from an alphabetical list for your region (by mailing address) and your operator class.
notes.explanation: It is how every new licensee gets a first call sign; you do not choose it.
notes.example: A new Technician is simply issued the next available call sign on the list for their region and class.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a vanity call sign, in one sentence?
notes.back: A call sign the FCC selects from a list of call signs you request, instead of the next one in sequence.
notes.explanation: Any licensee may apply for one, choosing from call signs for their own class or a lower one.
notes.example: A licensee who wants a more personal call sign lists up to 25 preferences and applies.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is station identification, in one sentence?
notes.back: Transmitting your call sign so that everyone receiving knows which station the transmissions come from.
notes.explanation: The rules require it regularly during and at the end of every communication, so listeners can tell which station is transmitting.
notes.example: Saying your call sign at the end of a conversation on a local frequency is station identification.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is Morse code, in one sentence?
notes.back: A code that sends each character as a pattern of short and long bursts of signal, called dots and dashes.
notes.explanation: The rules define international Morse code as a dot-dash code (97.3(a)(28)). Amateurs still send it by radio, and on some Technician band segments it is the only mode allowed.
notes.example: A dash lasts three times as long as a dot, and the characters are separated by a gap one dash long.
notes.source: 47 CFR 97.3(a)(28); NCVEC 2026–2030 Technician Pool, T8D09; US Navy, NEETS Module 12 (NAVEDTRA 14184), Modulation, p. 1-26
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US Government work)

notes.front: What is an emission, as the FCC rules define it?
notes.back: Radiation produced by a radio transmitting station, or the producing of it.
notes.explanation: The rules sort emissions into types, such as voice, Morse code and data, and say which types each band allows.
notes.example: Your voice going out from your handheld is an emission; the faint energy leaking from a receiver’s own circuits is not, because it is not a transmitting station.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: In the FCC rules, what does "phone" mean?
notes.back: Speech and other sound emissions: in short, voice transmissions.
notes.explanation: Rules on bands and identification say "phone" whenever they mean voice.
notes.example: Talking into a microphone on the air is phone; sending Morse code is not.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a phonetic alphabet, in one sentence?
notes.back: A standard set of words spoken in place of letters, so call signs and unusual words are received correctly.
notes.explanation: The rules encourage it for station identification by phone, and it is the standard way to spell out hard words.
notes.example: Spelling a call sign as one agreed word per letter, so a listener cannot mistake one similar-sounding letter for another, such as F for S.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is the licence grace period, in one sentence?
notes.back: The 2 years after a licence expires during which you may still apply to renew it.
notes.explanation: It rescues a forgotten renewal, but gives no permission to transmit until the renewal is granted.
notes.example: Your licence expired six months ago: you can still renew, but you must stay off the air until you do.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a club station licence, in one sentence?
notes.back: A station licence held for an amateur club by a trustee (the member named on it), who must hold an ordinary individual (operator/primary) licence.
notes.explanation: It lets a club run its own station with its own call sign, separate from any member's station.
notes.example: A local radio club with a name, members and a written organisation holds a club call sign, managed by its trustee.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a control operator, in one sentence?
notes.back: The amateur designated by a station's licensee to be responsible for that station's transmissions complying with the FCC rules.
notes.explanation: Every transmitting amateur station must have one, and the control operator's licence class sets the privileges used.
notes.example: When you operate your own station alone, the FCC presumes that you, the licensee, are its control operator.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: In the FCC rules, what is a space station?
notes.back: An amateur station located more than 50 km above the Earth's surface.
notes.explanation: The definition is about height, not about being a satellite or being crewed.
notes.example: An amateur station aboard a spacecraft in orbit is a space station.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a repeater, in one sentence?
notes.back: An amateur station that simultaneously retransmits another amateur station's signal on a different channel.
notes.explanation: Unlike an ordinary station, it sends out what it receives, at the same moment, on another channel.
notes.example: A handheld radio talks to a hilltop repeater, which retransmits the voice on another frequency across the area.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is an auxiliary station, in one sentence?
notes.back: An amateur station sending point-to-point communications within a system of cooperating amateur stations.
notes.explanation: It carries links inside a system, for example between parts of a repeater system, rather than talking to the public.
notes.example: A link that carries a remote receiver's audio back to a repeater is an auxiliary station.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a frequency coordinator, in one sentence?
notes.back: A local or regional body that recommends channels and settings for repeater and auxiliary stations to avoid interference.
notes.explanation: It is recognized by local amateurs whose stations are eligible to be repeater or auxiliary stations, not appointed by the FCC.
notes.example: Before putting up a new repeater, a club asks the area's frequency coordinator which channel to use.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a beacon station, in one sentence?
notes.back: An amateur station transmitting so that others can observe propagation and reception, or for related experiments.
notes.explanation: Hearing a known beacon tells you whether signals are getting through from its area.
notes.example: If you can hear a distant beacon on 10 meters, signals from that area are getting through on 10 meters right now.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is RACES, in one sentence?
notes.back: The Radio Amateur Civil Emergency Service: a radio service using amateur stations for civil defense communications during civil emergencies.
notes.explanation: It works through civil defense organizations, so taking part requires being enrolled with one.
notes.example: During a regional emergency, amateurs enrolled with the county civil defense organization pass its messages by radio.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Which skills does the Basis and Purpose of the amateur service say the rules should advance?
notes.back: Skills in both the communication and technical phases of the radio art.
notes.explanation: This is principle (c) of 97.1; others include emergency communications and international goodwill.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: According to its Basis and Purpose, what public value of the amateur service is singled out?
notes.back: Its value as a voluntary, noncommercial communication service, particularly for emergency communications.
notes.explanation: 97.1 lists five principles; (a) is the one about the service’s value to the public, and it singles out emergency communications.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What does 97.1 say about the amateur's ability to contribute to the radio art?
notes.back: It should be continued and extended.
notes.explanation: Principle (b) of 97.1: amateurs have a proven ability to advance the radio art.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What "reservoir" does 97.1 aim to expand?
notes.back: The reservoir of trained operators, technicians and electronics experts.
notes.explanation: Principle (d) of 97.1: the service is meant to keep adding trained people, which fits its definition as a service for self-training and technical investigation (97.3(a)(4)).
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Which unique ability of amateurs does 97.1 aim to continue and extend?
notes.back: Their ability to enhance international goodwill.
notes.explanation: Amateurs may talk directly with amateurs in other countries (97.117), and 97.1(e), the last of its five principles, names this goodwill as an ability to continue and extend.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Where are the FCC's amateur radio rules published?
notes.back: Title 47 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 97.
notes.explanation: The FCC regulates and enforces the service through these rules; exam rule questions cite them, e.g. 97.119.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Where do the rules list the places where the FCC regulates the amateur service?
notes.back: Appendix 1 to Part 97: the 50 states, DC, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands and certain Pacific islands.
notes.explanation: Examples in the Pacific include Guam and American Samoa, which are in ITU Region 3 (one of three world regions in the band tables); the Caribbean areas are in Region 2.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Do the FCC rules require a phonetic alphabet for station identification?
notes.back: No. It is encouraged, as an aid to correct identification, when identifying by phone.
notes.explanation: It is never required: not in emergencies, not with foreign stations, not anywhere. The rule only encourages it.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: After you pass, how does official notice of your new licence and call sign arrive?
notes.back: By email from the FCC, with a link to download the licence grant.
notes.explanation: Every licence grant must also show an email address where you can receive FCC correspondence (97.23).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What proves that the FCC has issued your licence grant?
notes.back: The licence appearing in the FCC's ULS database.
notes.explanation: The rules tie station operation and control operators to a grant appearing on the ULS database.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: After passing the exam for your first licence, when may you first transmit?
notes.back: As soon as your licence grant appears in the FCC's licence database (the ULS).
notes.explanation: Before that, you are not named in a licence grant on the ULS, which the rules require before a station may transmit.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: For how long does a CSCE give credit for the exam elements it shows?
notes.back: 365 days.
notes.explanation: Volunteer examiners must give credit for each element passed within the previous 365 days.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: For which licence classes does the FCC now issue new licences?
notes.back: Technician, General and Amateur Extra.
notes.explanation: Novice and Advanced still exist in the rules for older licensees, but no new grants are issued for them.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What happens when an old Technician Plus licence is renewed?
notes.back: It is renewed as a Technician Class licence.
notes.explanation: Technician Plus is not issued any more; the rules treat its renewal as a Technician renewal.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Who may apply for an operator/primary station licence?
notes.back: Anyone who qualifies by examination, except a representative of a foreign government.
notes.explanation: There is no age or citizenship test in this rule; the only exclusion is a foreign government representative.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Which licensees may apply for a vanity call sign?
notes.back: Any licensed amateur.
notes.explanation: Holders of an operator/primary licence (or a club trustee) are eligible, whatever their class.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: From which call signs may a vanity call sign be chosen?
notes.back: From the group for your own licence class or a lower one.
notes.explanation: A Technician cannot pick a call sign reserved for Amateur Extra licensees.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What may happen if FCC correspondence is undeliverable because your email address is wrong?
notes.back: Revocation of the station licence or suspension of the operator licence.
notes.explanation: Every licence grant must show a correct email address where you can receive FCC correspondence.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: May you operate your amateur station aboard a vessel in international waters?
notes.back: Yes, from a US-documented or registered vessel, with the master's approval.
notes.explanation: The rules extend a US licence to US-documented vessels, and the ship's master must approve the station.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is the normal term of an amateur licence?
notes.back: 10 years.
notes.explanation: The licence normally lasts 10 years, then must be renewed.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: How early before expiry may you apply to renew your licence?
notes.back: No sooner than 90 days before the expiration date (and no later than that date).
notes.explanation: The FCC's general wireless renewal rule, 1.949, sets this window for amateur licences too.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: How long is the grace period for renewing an expired licence?
notes.back: 2 years.
notes.explanation: After expiry you have 2 years to apply for renewal; after that the licence cannot be renewed.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: May you transmit during the grace period after your licence expires?
notes.back: No. No privileges are conferred until the licence is renewed.
notes.explanation: The grace period only keeps renewal open; operating must wait for the renewal grant.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What international communications may FCC-licensed amateurs make?
notes.back: Communications incidental to the purposes of the amateur service, and remarks of a personal character.
notes.explanation: Transmissions to other countries, where permitted, are limited to these two kinds.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is the minimum number of people for a club to hold a club station licence?
notes.back: At least four persons.
notes.explanation: The club also needs a name, a document of organization, management, and an amateur-service purpose.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: How high above the Earth must an amateur station be to count as a space station?
notes.back: More than 50 km above the Earth's surface.
notes.explanation: Below that, a station talking through satellites is an Earth station.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Who selects (recognizes) a frequency coordinator?
notes.back: Amateur operators in the local or regional area whose stations are eligible to be repeater or auxiliary stations.
notes.explanation: The FCC does not appoint coordinators; local amateurs recognize them.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Besides an FCC amateur licence, what must a RACES control operator have?
notes.back: Certification by a civil defense organization that they are enrolled in it.
notes.explanation: The station itself must also be registered with a civil defense organization.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What do the rules say about willful or malicious interference?
notes.back: No amateur operator may willfully or maliciously interfere with any radio communication or signal.
notes.explanation: It is an absolute ban, applying to any signal, amateur or not.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: On HF, where may an automatically controlled beacon transmit?
notes.back: On 10 meters, between 28.20 and 28.30 MHz.
notes.explanation: That is the only HF segment listed for automatic beacon control; the others are on VHF and above.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is the maximum transmitter power of a beacon?
notes.explanation: The 100 W limit applies to every beacon, whatever the band.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Which is a space station: an amateur station on a balloon 40 km up, or one on a craft 60 km up?
notes.back: The one 60 km up. Only stations more than 50 km above the Earth are space stations.
notes.explanation: The balloon station is within 50 km of the surface, so it is not a space station.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Your licence expires on 1 June. May you file for renewal on 1 February?
notes.back: No. That is about 120 days early; renewal may be filed no sooner than 90 days before expiry.
notes.explanation: From about 3 March until 1 June you may file.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: A licence was granted in September 2026. In what year does it normally expire?
notes.explanation: Amateur licences are normally granted for 10-year terms (97.25): 2026 + 10 = 2036.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Three friends form a radio club and want a club station licence. Can they get one?
notes.back: Not yet: a club must be composed of at least four persons.
notes.explanation: With a fourth member, plus a name, organizing document and management, they could apply.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: You passed your first exam today and hold a CSCE, but your grant is not yet in the ULS. May you transmit?
notes.back: No. You must wait until the grant appears in the ULS.
notes.explanation: A CSCE proves you passed; it does not license a first-time applicant to transmit.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: You passed the Technician exam 10 months ago and kept the CSCE. At a new exam session, must you pass that element again?
notes.back: No. The examiners must credit elements your CSCE shows as passed within the previous 365 days.
notes.explanation: After 365 days, the CSCE no longer gives that credit.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: A station keeps transmitting on top of a conversation on purpose to disrupt it. Which rule does this break?
notes.back: The ban on willful or malicious interference.
notes.explanation: No amateur may willfully or maliciously interfere with any radio communication or signal.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: During a contact with a station in another country, may you discuss your company's sales orders?
notes.back: No. International contacts are limited to amateur-service matters and personal remarks.
notes.explanation: Business is neither incidental to the amateur service's purposes nor a remark of a personal character.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Which of the following is part of the Basis and Purpose of the Amateur Radio Service?
notes.back: Advancing skills in the technical and communication phases of the radio art
notes.choices:
A) Providing personal radio communications for as many citizens as possible
B) Providing communications for international contesting
C) Advancing skills in the technical and communication phases of the radio art
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A: providing radio for as many citizens as possible is not among the five principles. B: international contesting is not a stated purpose. D: only C is correct.
notes.explanation: Principle (c) of 97.1 says the rules should advance skills in both the communication and technical phases of the art; the other options are not among its five principles. (47 CFR 97.1)
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Which agency regulates and enforces the rules for the Amateur Radio Service in the United States?
notes.back: The FCC
notes.choices:
A) ARRL
B) Homeland Security
C) The FCC
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A: the ARRL is not a government agency. B: Homeland Security does not regulate the service. D: only the FCC does.
notes.explanation: The amateur rules are the FCC’s own Part 97 of Title 47. The FCC grants the licences, and its representatives may inspect any station (97.103(c)). (47 CFR 97.1)
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What do the FCC rules state regarding the use of a phonetic alphabet for station identification in the Amateur Radio Service?
notes.back: It is encouraged when using phone emissions
notes.choices:
A) It is required when transmitting emergency messages
B) It is encouraged when using phone emissions
C) It is required when in contact with foreign stations
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A, C: the rule never requires it, in emergencies, foreign contacts or anywhere else. D: only B is correct.
notes.explanation: Phonetics help the listener get the call sign right, which is the point of identification (97.119(a)); the rule encourages them but stops short of requiring them (47 CFR 97.119(b)(2)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: How do you receive official notification of your new license and call sign after passing the exam?
notes.back: Email from the FCC with a link to download the license grant
notes.choices:
A) Email from the FCC with a link to download the license grant
B) USPS First-Class Mail from the FCC
C) Email from the lead volunteer examiner
D) USPS First-Class Mail from the lead volunteer examiner
notes.choicesExplained: B: official notice comes by email with a download link, not by post. C, D: the examiners do not issue the licence; the FCC does.
notes.explanation: The FCC emails you a link to download the licence grant, which is why a valid email address is required. (47 CFR 97.23)
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What proves that the FCC has issued an operator/primary license grant?
notes.back: The license appears in the FCC ULS database
notes.choices:
A) A printed copy of the certificate of successful completion of examination
B) An email notification from the NCVEC granting the license
C) The license appears in the FCC ULS database
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A: a CSCE shows exam elements passed, not a licence grant. B: the NCVEC does not grant licences. D: only C is correct.
notes.explanation: A licence exists when it appears in the FCC's ULS database. (47 CFR 97.7)
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: On which of the following HF frequencies can automatically controlled amateur propagation beacons be found?
notes.back: On ten meters, between 28.200 MHz and 28.300 MHz
notes.choices:
A) Anywhere in the Technician portion of 10 meters
B) Anywhere, if they are registered with the FCC
C) In a specific portion of each of the HF Technician bands
D) On ten meters, between 28.200 MHz and 28.300 MHz
notes.choicesExplained: A, C: automatic beacon control on HF is allowed only in 28.20–28.30 MHz. B: registration with the FCC is not the rule.
notes.explanation: Automatically controlled HF beacons are found on 10 meters, 28.200 to 28.300 MHz (47 CFR 97.203(d)), a slice of the 28.0–28.5 MHz that Technicians have on 10 m.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What is the FCC Part 97 definition of a space station?
notes.back: An amateur station located more than 50 km above Earth's surface
notes.choices:
A) Any satellite orbiting Earth
B) A manned satellite orbiting Earth
C) An amateur station located more than 50 km above Earth's surface
D) An amateur station using amateur radio satellites for relay of signals
notes.choicesExplained: A, B: being a satellite or crewed is not the test; height is. D: a station that uses satellites for relay is an Earth station.
notes.explanation: Height is the test because the rules split stations at 50 km: at or below 50 km, a station talking through satellites is an Earth station (97.3(a)(16)); above it, a space station (97.3(a)(41)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Who recommends transmit/receive channels for repeater and auxiliary stations?
notes.back: A Volunteer Frequency Coordinator recognized by local amateurs
notes.choices:
A) A Frequency Spectrum Manager appointed by the FCC
B) A Volunteer Frequency Coordinator recognized by local amateurs
C) An FCC Regional Field Office
D) The International Telecommunication Union
notes.choicesExplained: A, C: the FCC does not appoint or act as coordinator. D: the ITU does not recommend local repeater channels.
notes.explanation: The coordinator recommends channels and technical settings so that repeater and auxiliary stations avoid or minimize interference. It is recognized by local amateurs, not appointed by the FCC (47 CFR 97.3(a)(22)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Who selects a Frequency Coordinator?
notes.back: Amateur operators in a local or regional area whose stations are eligible to be repeater or auxiliary stations
notes.choices:
A) The FCC Office of Spectrum Management and Coordination Policy
B) The local chapter of the Office of National Council of Independent Frequency Coordinators
C) Amateur operators in a local or regional area whose stations are eligible to be repeater or auxiliary stations
D) The FCC Regional Field Office
notes.choicesExplained: A, B, D: coordinators are not chosen by the FCC or a national council; local amateurs recognize them.
notes.explanation: The rule defines the coordinator as recognized by the amateur operators in the area whose stations are eligible to be repeater or auxiliary stations: the stations it coordinates choose it (47 CFR 97.3(a)(22)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Besides an FCC-issued amateur operator license, what is required to be the control operator of a Radio Amateur Civil Emergency Service (RACES) Station?
notes.back: Certification of current enrollment by a civil defense organization
notes.choices:
A) A written recommendation by the local ARRL Emergency Coordinator
B) Membership in the Amateur Radio Emergency Service (ARES)
C) Certification of current enrollment by a civil defense organization
D) Nothing
notes.choicesExplained: A: no ARRL recommendation is required. B: ARES membership is not the RACES requirement. D: something more is required.
notes.explanation: The rule requires two things: an FCC-issued amateur licence and certification by a civil defense organization that you are enrolled in it (47 CFR 97.407(a)). RACES messages must be authorized by that organization (97.407(d)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Which of the following is prohibited?
notes.back: Willful or malicious interference
notes.choices:
A) International communications on VHF bands and higher frequencies
B) Willful or malicious interference
C) Third-party traffic using digital modes
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A: international contacts on VHF and above are allowed. C: 97.115 permits messages for third parties, with no ban tied to digital modes. D: only B is correct.
notes.explanation: No amateur operator may willfully or maliciously interfere with any radio communication. (47 CFR 97.101(d))
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: For which classes of amateur radio licenses does the FCC currently issue new licenses?
notes.back: Technician, General, Amateur Extra
notes.choices:
A) Novice, Technician, General, Amateur Extra
B) Technician, Technician Plus, General, Amateur Extra
C) Novice, Technician Plus, General, Advanced
D) Technician, General, Amateur Extra
notes.choicesExplained: A, C: no new Novice or Advanced licences are issued. B: Technician Plus is not issued; it is renewed as Technician.
notes.explanation: 97.9(a) lists five classes, but 97.17(a) says no new Novice or Advanced licences will be issued, which leaves Technician, General and Amateur Extra.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Who may select a desired call sign under the vanity call sign rules?
notes.back: Any licensed amateur
notes.choices:
A) Only a licensed amateur with a General or Amateur Extra Class license
B) Only a licensed amateur with an Amateur Extra Class license
C) Only a licensed amateur who has been licensed continuously for more than 10 years
D) Any licensed amateur
notes.choicesExplained: A, B, C: the vanity system is not limited by class or by years licensed.
notes.explanation: Anyone named in an operator/primary (or club) licence may apply (97.19(a)); class matters only for which call signs you may pick, from your own class group or lower (97.19(d)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What types of international communications are FCC-licensed amateur radio stations permitted to make?
notes.back: Communications incidental to the purposes of the Amateur Radio Service and remarks of a personal character
notes.choices:
A) Communications incidental to the purposes of the Amateur Radio Service and remarks of a personal character
B) Communications incidental to conducting business or remarks of a personal nature
C) Only communications incidental to contest exchanges; all other communications are prohibited
D) Any communications that would be permitted by an international broadcast station
notes.choicesExplained: B: business communications are not permitted. C: contacts are not limited to contests. D: amateurs are not broadcasters; international contacts have their own limits.
notes.explanation: Communications for hire or on behalf of an employer are banned for all amateur stations (97.113(a)(2), (3)). For other countries, 97.117 also limits contacts to matters incidental to the service and personal remarks. (47 CFR 97.117)
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What may happen if the FCC is unable to reach you by email?
notes.back: Revocation of the station license or suspension of the operator license
notes.choices:
A) Fine and suspension of operator license
B) Revocation of the station license or suspension of the operator license
C) Revocation of access to the license record in the FCC system
D) Nothing; there is no such requirement
notes.choicesExplained: A: the rule names revocation or suspension, not a fine. C: not what the rule says. D: the email requirement exists.
notes.explanation: An undeliverable email address can lead to revocation of the station licence or suspension of the operator licence. (47 CFR 97.23)
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Which of the following is a valid Group D call sign format for Technician class?
notes.back: KF1XXX
notes.choices:
A) KF1XXX
B) KA1X
C) W1XX
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: B, C: the pool does not key these as the Technician Group D format. D: only A is correct.
notes.explanation: The pool keys KF1XXX (two letters, a numeral, three letters) as a Technician Group D format. Sequential call signs are grouped by class and region; the group formats come from the FCC’s call-sign system, which this deck has not checked beyond the pool.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Which of the following statements is true about using your amateur radio license when operating aboard a vessel or craft in international waters?
notes.back: You may operate from a US-documented vessel with the master's permission
notes.choices:
A) Amateur operation is prohibited in international waters
B) You may only operate during maritime emergencies
C) You need special FCC authorization for maritime mobile operation
D) You may operate from a US-documented vessel with the master's permission
notes.choicesExplained: A: operation is allowed on a US-documented vessel. B: not only during emergencies. C: no special FCC authorization; the master's approval is what is needed.
notes.explanation: A US licence covers a US-documented vessel, and the ship's master must approve the station. (47 CFR 97.5(a)(2), 97.11(a))
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: How long before the expiration date may an amateur radio license renewal be requested?
notes.back: 90 days
notes.choices:
A) 30 days
B) 90 days
C) 6 months
D) 1 year
notes.choicesExplained: A: you may renew 30 days before expiry, but you may start as early as 90 days before, which is what the question asks. C, D: too early; filing more than 90 days ahead is not allowed.
notes.explanation: Renewals follow 47 CFR 1.949(a) (via 97.21), which requires filing no later than the expiration date and no sooner than 90 days before it.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What is the normal term for an FCC-issued amateur radio license?
notes.back: Ten years
notes.choices:
A) Five years
B) Eight years
C) Ten years
D) Life
notes.choicesExplained: A, B: shorter than the actual term. D: licences are not for life.
notes.explanation: The rule sets the normal term at 10 years (47 CFR 97.25); renewal, filed up to 90 days before expiry, gives another term.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What is the grace period for renewal if an amateur license expires?
notes.back: Two years
notes.choices:
A) Two years
B) Three years
C) Five years
D) Ten years
notes.choicesExplained: B, C, D: longer than the rule allows.
notes.explanation: An expired licence may be renewed within a 2-year grace period. (47 CFR 97.21(b))
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: How soon after passing the examination for your first amateur radio license may you transmit on the amateur radio bands?
notes.back: As soon as your operator/station license grant appears in the FCC’s license database
notes.choices:
A) Immediately on receiving your Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination (CSCE)
B) As soon as your operator/station license grant appears on the ARRL website
C) As soon as your operator/station license grant appears in the FCC’s license database
D) As soon as you receive your license in the mail from the FCC
notes.choicesExplained: A: a CSCE alone does not let a first-time licensee transmit. B: the ARRL website is not the licence database. D: waiting for a paper licence is not the test; you may transmit once the grant is in the FCC’s database, and official notice comes by email.
notes.explanation: A station may transmit only when a person named in a licence grant on the ULS database controls it (47 CFR 97.5(a)); a first-time licensee has no grant until it appears there.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: If your license has expired and is still within the allowable grace period, may you continue to transmit on the amateur radio bands?
notes.back: No, you must wait until the license has been renewed
notes.choices:
A) Yes, for up to two years
B) Yes, as soon as you apply for renewal
C) Yes, for up to one year
D) No, you must wait until the license has been renewed
notes.choicesExplained: A, B, C: no privileges are conferred during the grace period until the renewal is granted.
notes.explanation: An expired licence confers no privileges until it is renewed, even within the grace period. (47 CFR 97.21(b))
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Which of the following is a requirement for the issuance of a club station license grant?
notes.back: The club must have at least four members
notes.choices:
A) The trustee must have an Amateur Extra Class operator license grant
B) The club must have at least four members
C) The club must be registered with the American Radio Relay League (ARRL)
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A: the trustee needs an operator/primary licence, of any class. C: no ARRL registration is required. D: only B is correct.
notes.explanation: The rule sets a minimum size and some structure: at least four persons, a name, a document of organization, management, and a primary purpose devoted to amateur activities (47 CFR 97.5(b)(2)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Licence term, grace period, renewal window, CSCE credit: which one lasts 90 days?
notes.back: The renewal window: you may file no sooner than 90 days before expiry.
notes.explanation: Term 10 years; grace period 2 years; renewal window 90 days; CSCE credit 365 days.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Sequential or vanity: in which system do you choose your call sign?
notes.back: Vanity: the FCC picks from your list. Sequential: the FCC assigns the next one for your region and class.
notes.explanation: Every new licensee starts with a sequential call sign; a vanity call sign is an optional change.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Repeater or auxiliary station: which simultaneously retransmits another station's signal on a different channel?
notes.back: The repeater. An auxiliary station sends point-to-point links within a system of cooperating stations.
notes.explanation: A repeater serves users on the air; an auxiliary station carries links inside a system, such as to a repeater.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: CSCE or ULS grant: which one lets a first-time licensee go on the air?
notes.back: The grant appearing in the ULS. A CSCE only proves exam elements passed.
notes.explanation: The CSCE comes the day you pass; the transmitting privilege begins when the grant is in the database.
notes.source: NCVEC 2026–2030 Technician Pool, T1C10, T1A05; 47 CFR 97.3(a)(15), 97.5(a)
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain
